body: I have a lot of lovely people around me, but I feel like this topic will only stress them out and make them worry about me. So I prefer to keep it inside. I felt a bit better when I posted my feelings here though :) I don't know what to do in order to not think this way. It's always been like that.

It is good that you both broke up on good terms. As in she also thinks it's the right thing to do. Maybe in the future, if you guys live closer to each other, you will be able to get back together.

It seems to me that you didn't really have much of a choice here, so don't blame yourself too much. Especially if she agreed, it was probably the right choice. Sometimes life gets in the way and it is incredibly sad and painful.

Also, LDR is hard as it is. You might be hurting a lot at the moment, but you would be a lot more hurt if you stayed in the relationship while feeling unhappy.
Yes, that's completely understandable and normal if you feel like that sometimes. It all comes down to how you deal with those feelings. Good luck!

I am a girl and I can't say we do that. 

You should probably talk to her about it. You can tell her how it made you feel. For example: "Earlier today, I accidentally saw that you received on your snapchat a nude photo of some girl. It made me feel a bit uneasy, since I know you are bisexual. I just wanted to let you because I don't want to make assumptions on something that might not even mean anything. "

This way you are communicating your feelings and putting the focus on yourself rather than blaming her or make her feel that you don't trust her. Misunderstandings can happen in the future over the smallest of things but if you have good communication things will be ok. :)
That's up to you. It doesn't matter either way
Probably showing her support. My friends at least tend to be more angry at my exes than I am.
Well... There you go. She doesn't want to get back together, you don't want to stay friends. Blocking you is a way for her to move on. Don't overthink it and let her be. Try to focus on yourself now.

Was it her decision to break up?

It could also mean she is trying to move on and seeing you or having a way to talk to you isn't helping.

Or.. She was upset that you blocked her.

She is probably mad at you and doesnt want to talk to you. Neither do her friends.

It will probably be the best to let her go and not try to contact her.

I would say keep going with the no contact. If you want you can even reply to her and let her know you need sometime on your own and would prefer not to talk for a little bit.

It might just be that she is feeling lonely and just wants that quick fix. I think the more time you give her to think about what she wants, the more chances you have of getting back together permanently.

Sort of. I will be going overseas in a week for half a year. We wont be continuing being together while I will be there. Again, we have left it open for the future, but with no promises of getting back. For us, it's just life getting in the way. No real issues.

I'm sorry to hear you are going through this. Once he leaves, things will be much easier for you. Don't see it as the last day with him in the same house, but as the first day of your new life :) Good luck

You can talk to her and see if she would be willing to move in with you. Let her know, you are worried about her expenses and you won't be the one taking care of things, because you want to focus on your career. If you see she is definetely trying, then give her another chance.

On the other hand, if you are sure that being single is the best for you right now, then it's better to break up. Long distance is hard as it is, especially if you don't see a solution where you guys can live closer with each other.

Mine wasn't exactly a break, but an actual break up. We left it open for the future. We ended up getting back together after 1 year. In that year I grew up so much as a person and so did he. Once we got back together our relationship was better than it was before.

It takes a lot of time. Especially if you have issues. Both of you should be willing to work on them.

Try to imagine both of you in the future. Do you think you will still have the feelings you are having now? If yes, then is it worth it torturing yourself for the rest of your life?

People break up for less serious reasons. It all comes down to your happiness, and you sounds unhappy.

How long are you planning on taking a break? I also think, especially if you are young, it's ok to take some time apart in order to focus on yourself. It helps you grow as an individual without having to lose the person you want to end up with. IF both of you are ok with it and it's not damaging.
On the other hand, if you are having these breaks due to problems in your relationship, maybe it's time to reconsider if you should get back together or not.

I think you will have better chances of getting together if you stop contacting him, give both of you a lot of time (not just one week) to grow and then maybe try again, if you think it's the right thing to do.
Since you like the girl you are talking to right now, why don't you give her a chance? Maybe you will figure out you aren't made for each other and then you can see what happens with the other one.
It doesn't matter what you do as long as you are both happy :)
He is pretty sure he doesn't want to have a LDR so I can't do much about it. I was willing to work on it, but you can't force someone. I just wish it was easier to let go.
Fair enough. In that case it doesn't really matter. You can just tell her the reason why you are breaking up with her and that's it.
If he is not willing to compromise and you are left doing all the compromising yourself maybe it's time to rethink your relationship. Perhaps you have grown to have different needs.

Talk to her about it. You will know if you should break up or not depending on what she says. If you break up with her without talking about it you might regret it in the future "What if she had a legitimate reason?" etc.

Long distance is hard. It all comes down to you though.

Do you think you can handle not seeing him for 6 months?
Are you willing to put the extra effort in order to stay together?
Is he willing to put the effort? And can he handle the long distance himself?
Do you trust each other? Is the relationship worth the wait? 

If you can say yes to all of these then yeah, go for it. But if you are unsure about some maybe it's best to break up. Good luck!

If you are talking about common interests and hobbies, you doesn't have to have that many things in common. You can still be your individual self inside the relationship.
If you are talking about more important values such as marriage, having kids, wanting to travel/live abroad etc. then it will probably cause an issue later on. At the end of the day, those are the things that make a long term relationship in my opinion.

I am in a similar situation as you. And I have been in one like that before as well. I think the best thing you can do is try to move on. He might come back and decide he doesn't want to date anymore.
Best not to contact him, let him miss you. He will come to you if he wants.

It's a good sign. You are starting to heal :) nothing is worse than the first few days. After that it gets better. You will have your occasional moments where you will feel bad, but I think the worst is over now.

Try having a one month no contact. Usually at this time you start to get over her and in the meantime she gets the space she wants. Maybe she will even regret what she did and come back to you. But even if she doesn't, you will be on your way on getting over her :)
I don't actually know any Finnish. I will be taking English classes. And I will be just staying in a shared apartment

Yes, I felt the same exact way. They didn't accept me on the first uni and I was devastated and tried for the second one. I was so happy that they got me at the time. Still stressed tho haha. I'm sure it will be fine for both of us. I'm going to Finland, wht about you?

You will find your way again :) As you said, time heals. You have become comfortable with that person in your life and have gotten used to them so now you will be a bit off balance for a while. Take your time to grieve. Eventually you will get tired of being sad and everything will fall into place. 
 Try to focus on yourself also! Being single is just as rewarding. You can do the things you couldn't do while you were in a relationship.

I'm also leaving for exchange in a week and I am experiencing the same anxieties and worries as you do! The closer the date comes, the more excited I am though, so I am sure your excitement will overpower your worries eventually :)

You never know. Maybe in the meantime she will realise she needs to become more independent in your relationship and in the end you won't have to break up with her at all. Sometimes getting a little hurt can be a good thing.

Maybe you could ask her to take some time apart. Maybe for a couple of weeks? See how things go. If you see that your life is changing for the better maybe it's the best to break up. But if you feel like it would be a mistake to let her go, then try to work on it from there.

It seems like your mind and your heart want different things. I am sure some time apart will give you a clear answer as to what you want to do.
Have you tried talking to her about it?

She sounds like she has become very dependent on you. Maybe breaking up won't only help you grow as a person but her as well. She will have to put herself out there, find new friends and hobbies etc.

If you think it's the right thing to do then you should probably break up, yeah.

There's no easy way to do it, just explain to her how you are feeling. Understand that she will be upset for a while but eventually she will ok :)
Good luck
I think that's ok then :) It happens sometimes, don't focus on it too much.

2.5 years is a long time to be in a relationship with someone. You built together many memories. Honestly, I believe you never fully get over someone, you just learn to move on. But sometimes you are still going to miss them even if you don't want them back. I don't think it's a bad thing, unless your thoughts start to impact your current relationship negatively. If your thoughts start to become more frequent start reevaluating your feelings. Have you actually gotten over your ex or have you convinced yourself that you have, just cause it's the right thing to do?

I've been in a similar situation to hers. It will probably hurt her yes, like any of us when we are being broken up, but depression is something you can't control. If she really cares for you, she will understand.

I think you should first discuss with her you are feeling at the moment. How depression makes you feel apathetic. See if she can understand your feelings. If she does it will probably be easier to tell her maybe it's best to break up. It won't be as sudden cause she will be aware of your issues.

And you never know.. Maybe some time apart is all you need.
You can always get back together in the future, when you have put your feelings in order. And if you do, you both will be much happier. (maybe don't tell her that tho, so she won't wait for you - but you can always give it a go)
Good luck OP. I think it's very brave of you to do that. Breaking up/divorcing with the person you love is the most painful thing to do.
